name: Delhi
tagline: Mughal tombs, colonial avenues and old bazaars
description: India's capital layers several historic cities on top of each other: Mughal forts and garden tombs, the wide avenues of New Delhi, and some of the busiest markets in the country.

name: Agra
tagline: The Taj Mahal and the riverside Mughal city
description: Once a Mughal capital on the Yamuna, Agra holds the Taj Mahal, the red-sandstone Agra Fort and a string of riverside tombs and gardens.

name: Jaipur
tagline: The Pink City of forts, palaces and observatories
description: Rajasthan's capital, planned in the 18th century, with a walled pink old city, hilltop forts on the Aravalli ridge and a UNESCO-listed astronomical observatory.

name: Varanasi
tagline: Ghats, temples and evening aarti on the Ganga
description: One of the world's oldest continuously inhabited cities, built along the ghats of the Ganga, with Sarnath, where the Buddha first taught, just to the north.

name: Ayodhya
description: An ancient pilgrimage city on the Saryu river, revered as the birthplace of Rama, with the new Ram Mandir, old temples and riverside ghats.

name: Tirupati
description: A temple city at the foot of the Seshachalam hills; the road up to the Venkateswara temple at Tirumala starts here.

name: Mumbai
tagline: Colonial landmarks and a sea-facing skyline
description: India's largest city, with Victorian and Art Deco landmarks in the south, the Arabian Sea promenade of Marine Drive and busy markets.

name: Calangute
description: A beach town on the coast of North Goa, close to Baga, Candolim and the Portuguese-era Fort Aguada.

name: Amritsar
tagline: The Golden Temple and the border ceremony
description: The spiritual centre of Sikhism, home to the Golden Temple, with the Partition-era memorials of the old city and the Attari–Wagah border nearby.

name: Udaipur
tagline: The city of lakes and palaces
description: Former capital of Mewar, built around Lake Pichola and Fateh Sagar, with the lakeside City Palace and island palaces.

name: Haridwar
tagline: Where the Ganga leaves the mountains
description: A Hindu pilgrimage city where the Ganga enters the plains, known for the evening aarti at Har Ki Pauri and its hilltop temples.

name: Rishikesh
description: A town on the Ganga in the Himalayan foothills, known for ashrams, yoga, river rafting and its footbridges across the river.

name: Vrindavan
description: A town on the Yamuna associated with Krishna's childhood, with thousands of temples from old shrines to large modern ones.

name: Mathura
tagline: Birthplace of Krishna on the Yamuna
description: One of India's oldest cities, revered as Krishna's birthplace, with riverside ghats and a museum of early Indian sculpture.

name: Shirdi
description: A pilgrimage town in Maharashtra that grew around the life and shrine of the saint Sai Baba of Shirdi.

name: Katra
tagline: Base town for the Vaishno Devi trek
description: The town at the foot of the Trikuta hills where the pilgrimage trek to the Vaishno Devi shrine begins.

name: Ujjain
tagline: Ancient city of the Mahakal temple
description: An ancient city on the Shipra river, home to the Mahakaleshwar Jyotirlinga and host of the Simhastha Kumbh Mela.

name: Manali
tagline: Mountain resort in the Kullu valley
description: A Himalayan resort town on the Beas river, the starting point for Solang Valley, Rohtang Pass and the Atal Tunnel.

name: Shimla
description: Capital of Himachal Pradesh and the summer capital of British India, with the Ridge, Mall Road and colonial buildings on its hills.

name: Prayagraj
description: The city of the Triveni Sangam, the confluence of the Ganga and Yamuna, host of the Kumbh Mela and of the Nehru family's Anand Bhavan.

name: Ajmer
tagline: The dargah city by Ana Sagar
description: A city in the Aravalli hills known for the Sufi shrine of Moinuddin Chishti, the artificial lake Ana Sagar and early Indo-Islamic monuments.

name: Hyderabad
description: Capital of Telangana, founded by the Qutb Shahi dynasty, with the Charminar, Golconda Fort and the palaces of the Nizams.

name: Kochi
tagline: Spice port of the Malabar coast
description: A historic port city whose Fort Kochi and Mattancherry districts keep Portuguese, Dutch, Jewish and British heritage.

name: Munnar
tagline: Tea hills of the Western Ghats
description: A hill station in Kerala surrounded by tea estates, close to Eravikulam National Park and the high viewpoints of the Ghats.

name: Alleppey
description: Alappuzha sits between the Arabian Sea and the Kerala backwaters, known for its canals, beaches and houseboat trips.

name: Sabarimala
description: A forest hill shrine in the Western Ghats, reached on foot from the Pamba base; visits follow the temple's seasonal calendar.

name: Madurai
tagline: The temple city of Tamil Nadu
description: One of the oldest cities of South India, built around the Meenakshi Amman Temple and its towering gopurams.

name: Chennai
description: Capital of Tamil Nadu, with the long Marina Beach, Fort St. George and the old temple quarter of Mylapore.

name: Rameswaram
description: A pilgrimage town on Pamban Island, home to the Ramanathaswamy Temple and the road to Dhanushkodi.

name: Kanyakumari
description: The southernmost town of mainland India, where three seas meet, known for its sunrises and the rock memorials offshore.

name: Ooty
description: A hill station in the Nilgiri mountains with a lake, botanical and rose gardens and the Nilgiri Mountain Railway.

name: Bengaluru
description: Karnataka's capital, known for its parks, the granite Vidhana Soudha and a busy café and shopping scene.

name: Mysuru
description: The former royal capital of Mysore, famous for its palace, the Dasara festival and Chamundi Hill.

name: Hampi
description: The ruins of the Vijayanagara capital, a UNESCO World Heritage Site of temples and royal buildings among boulder hills.

name: Puri
description: A coastal pilgrimage city in Odisha, home to the Jagannath Temple and its annual Ratha Yatra.

name: Konark
tagline: The Sun Temple by the sea
description: A coastal town in Odisha known for the 13th-century Konark Sun Temple, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

name: Kolkata
description: The former capital of British India, with the Victoria Memorial, the Howrah Bridge and a deep tradition of museums and culture.

name: Darjeeling
description: A hill town in West Bengal known for its tea, the Darjeeling Himalayan Railway and sunrise views of Kangchenjunga.

name: Srinagar
description: The summer capital of Jammu and Kashmir, known for Dal Lake, its houseboats and the terraced Mughal gardens.

name: Leh
description: The main town of Ladakh at about 3,500 m, with a royal palace, monasteries and stupas in a high desert valley.

name: Jodhpur
description: A city on the edge of the Thar Desert, overlooked by Mehrangarh Fort, with blue-painted houses in its old quarter.

name: Jaisalmer
tagline: The Golden City of the Thar
description: A desert city with a living sandstone fort, carved havelis and the dunes of Sam to the west.

name: Pushkar
tagline: Sacred lake and the Brahma temple
description: A small pilgrimage town around a sacred lake, known for its rare Brahma temple, ghats and the annual Pushkar fair.

name: Nainital
description: A hill station built around a lake in the Kumaon hills, with viewpoints over the Himalaya.

name: Mussoorie
tagline: Queen of the hills above Dehradun
description: A hill station on a ridge above the Doon valley, known for Mall Road, walking roads and waterfalls nearby.

name: Kedarnath
description: A high Himalayan pilgrimage town, reached by a 16 km trek from Gaurikund, open only part of the year.

name: Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar (Aurangabad)
description: A city in Maharashtra, officially renamed Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, and the base for the Ajanta and Ellora caves.

name: Khajuraho
description: A small town known for its 10th–12th-century Hindu and Jain temples, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

name: Kevadia (Ekta Nagar)
tagline: Statue of Unity on the Narmada
description: A town on the Narmada river, now called Ekta Nagar, built around the Statue of Unity and the Sardar Sarovar Dam.

name: Pondicherry
tagline: French quarter on the Coromandel coast
description: The former French colony of Puducherry, with a seafront promenade, the Sri Aurobindo Ashram and Auroville nearby.
